# @mission-platform/forge-web-script

Forge Web Script v1 language contracts, bootstrap parser, and conformance fixtures.

The authoritative language and capability reference is `docs/forge-web-script.md`
at the repository root. The public API exports AST, lexer, parser, diagnostics,
ABI manifest, compiler artifact contracts, and bootstrap validation helpers.

## Installation

Add it to a consuming workspace member:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@mission-platform/forge-web-script": "workspace:*"
  }
}
```

## Usage

```ts
import { validateForgeWebScript } from '@mission-platform/forge-web-script';

const result = validateForgeWebScript(source, 'runtime.fws', {
  requestedCapabilities: ['clock.now'],
});
```

Tooling consumers use `createForgeWebScriptCompilerService` with the bounded
self-hosted lex stage enabled by default. The CLI exposes the stage mode as
`--vm-mode interpret|jit|aot`; Vite and language-service integrations use
`selfHostedVmMode`. The lex stage is VM-executed and parity-checked against the
seed, while later compiler stages remain explicitly seed-backed until their own
bootstrap parity is complete. Wasm remains the production artifact path.

## Iterator and explicit outcomes

FWS uses `Option<T>` and `Result<T, E>` from the standard library instead of
source-language exceptions. Match every outcome explicitly:

```fws
fn is_present<T>(value: Option<T>) -> bool {
  match value {
    Option::None => false,
    Option::Some(_) => true,
  }
}

export iter fn values(source: Iterator<i32>) -> Iterator<i32> {
  loop next = source.next() { yield next; }
}
```

`iter fn` exports are adapted to JavaScript iterators. The generated export has
`next()` returning `{ value, done }`, remains complete after the first done
result, and can be consumed by `for...of` in JavaScript. `throw`, `try`,
`catch`, `for`, `while`, and `do while` are rejected by the frontend.

## Optimization, target profiles, and debug artifacts

Release compilation may unroll proven empty iterators, inline pure calls, and
identify tail calls. Mark a function `noinline` when its call boundary must be
preserved; host capability calls remain observable and are not reordered.
Target capabilities are explicit compile input and become part of the ABI
manifest and cache identity:

```ts
compileForgeWebScript({
  source,
  fileName: 'runtime.fws',
  compilerVersion: '0.1.0',
  optimization: 'release',
  targetFeatures: { simd: true, tailCall: true, memory64: true },
  compilerHints: { iteratorUnrollLimit: 4 },
});
```

Threads require both `threads: true` and `atomics: true`; unsupported feature
combinations produce diagnostics instead of silently downgrading. When a WAT
cache is configured, debug compilation writes deterministic
`<key>.optimized.wat`, `<key>.unoptimized.wat`, `<key>.optimized.wasm`, and
`<key>.unoptimized.wasm` companions when the cache provides a binary writer.
Cache failures are logged and do not fail compilation.
